passages.note: The bill page shows Smaltz as author and prints the digest, not the operative text.

passages.provision_quote: Sec. 1. The First Congressional District consists of the following:
passages.note: The bill enacts congressional districts by statute and limits interim judicial relief, but keeps supreme court review and names no partisan-bias standard.
House third-reading passage, 57-41, so not near-unanimous; the page prints no provision.

rows.reasoning: Smaltz authored HB 1032 (2026), which draws congressional districts in statute ("Sec. 1. The First Congressional District consists of the following:"), lets the general assembly amend them outside the post-census session, and restricts interim relief in apportionment suits; he also voted Yea on its House passage, 57-41. That places him on the legislature-draws side but does not match "state legislatures with court oversight to prevent extreme partisan bias", since the bill sets no partisan-bias standard, nor "the party that controls the state legislature without outside interference", since SECTION 3 preserves supreme court jurisdiction over apportionment appeals rather than removing court review.
